# Contributing to reiod

Thank you for taking the time to contribute. This file explains how to report a
problem, how to propose a change, and the one rule that is specific to this
package: **the cut-off values are not ours to change**.

## Code of conduct

Please note that this package is released with a
[Contributor Code of Conduct](https://ropensci.org/code-of-conduct/). By
contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.

## Reporting a problem

Open an issue at <https://github.com/nicholustintzaw/reiod/issues>. The most
useful reports include:

* a **minimal reproducible example**, ideally with
  [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/). The shipped `eiod_demo` data is a
  good starting point, and avoids sharing your own survey data;
* the output of `sessionInfo()`;
* what you expected to happen, and what happened instead.

**Do not attach survey microdata** or anything that could identify a
respondent or household. If a problem only shows with your data, reproduce it
on `eiod_demo` or on a few made-up values.

If the issue is about a **result** (a classification you believe is wrong),
please include the indicator, the demographic group, the value, and the cut-off
it was compared with, from `eiod_lookup_cutoff()`. Most such reports turn out
to be a unit mismatch; `eiod_check_data()` usually finds it.

## Proposing a change

Small fixes (typos, documentation wording) can go straight to a pull request.
For anything larger, please open an issue first, so we can agree on the
approach before you spend time on it.

1. Fork the repository and create a branch from `main`.
2. Make your change. Edit the roxygen comments in `R/`, never the files in
   `man/` or `NAMESPACE`, which are generated by `devtools::document()`. Edit
   `README.Rmd`, not `README.md`, then re-knit it with
   `devtools::build_readme()`.
3. Add or update tests in `tests/testthat/` for any change in behaviour.
4. Run `devtools::test()` and `devtools::check()`. Both should pass with no
   errors or warnings.
5. Add a bullet to the top section of `NEWS.md` describing the change from a
   user's point of view.
6. Open a pull request against `main`, explaining what changed and why.

`tools/build.R` lists the full rebuild sequence.

### Style

* Function and argument names are `snake_case`. Every exported object starts
  with `eiod_`.
* The package has no dependencies beyond base R (`stats` and `utils`). Please
  do not add a package to `Imports` without discussing it in an issue first;
  packages used only in tests or vignettes go in `Suggests`.
* Functions take plain vectors (`df$column`), not unquoted column names.
* Report problems with `stop()`, `warning()` or `message()`; use `cat()` only
  inside `print()` methods.

## The cut-off values

The 616 cut-offs in `data-raw/eiod_cutoffs.csv` are transcribed from Intake's
methods paper, *Methods for Assessing Healthy, Environmentally Sustainable
Diets Globally* (Tables 3 and 4a–4g). Eight Table 3 eutrophication values carry
a correction supplied by Intake and are marked in the `value_source` column.

**These values change only on Intake's instruction**: a revised paper, or a
written correction from Intake. A pull request that edits a cut-off must cite
that source. If you believe a value is wrong, please open an issue rather than
a pull request, quoting the table, row and column, and what the paper prints.

When a value does change:

* edit `data-raw/eiod_cutoffs.csv` only, then rebuild with
  `source("data-raw/build_data.R")`. The script stops if any value no longer
  round-trips to its published digits;
* `tests/testthat/test-reference_values.R` compares cut-offs against values
  typed by hand from the paper, so it needs updating in the same pull request;
* the same CSV is shared with the companion Stata package
  [eiod](https://github.com/nicholustintzaw/eiod), so a change there is needed
  too.

## Acknowledgement

Contributors are credited in `NEWS.md`. People who make a substantial
contribution to the code or documentation are added to `Authors@R` in
`DESCRIPTION`, with their agreement.
